**Setup (Bayes' theorem):**

- Prevalence: P(D) = 1/500 = 0.002, so P(¬D) = 0.998
- Sensitivity: P(+|D) = 0.98
- Specificity: P(−|¬D) = 0.95, so P(+|¬D) = 0.05 (false positive rate)

**Total probability of testing positive:**

P(+) = P(+|D)·P(D) + P(+|¬D)·P(¬D)
P(+) = (0.98 × 0.002) + (0.05 × 0.998)
P(+) = 0.00196 + 0.0499
P(+) = 0.05186

**Applying Bayes' theorem:**

P(D|+) = P(+|D)·P(D) / P(+) = 0.00196 / 0.05186 ≈ 0.0377941

**Sanity check:** Out of 500,000 people — 1,000 have the disease (982 test positive), 499,000 don't (24,950 false positives). Positive total = 982 + 24,950 = 25,932. True positives/total positives = 982/25,932 ≈ 0.037882... 

Let me redo this check precisely with exact fractions to make sure rounding didn't creep in: using 500 as denominator directly — per 500 people, 1 has disease (0.98 expected positive), 499 don't (499×0.05 = 24.95 expected false positives). Positive total = 0.98 + 24.95 = 25.93. Ratio = 0.98/25.93 = 0.0377941...

This matches the earlier calculation: 0.00196/0.05186 = 0.0377941... → **3.78%**

FINAL ANSWER: 3.78
